title: Cross-architecture & sequence-length Bayesian kernel selection probe
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Build a lightweight Bayesian probe-and-adapt system that recommends kernel implementations per request based on GPU architecture fingerprint and sequence-length bucket. Unlike deterministic heuristics, this ticket explores probabilistic priors updated with small microbench probes and production telemetry so the runtime can prefer low-regret kernels under shifting load and model mixes. The design separates prefill vs decode regimes, maintains calibrated uncertainty, and enforces safety budgets for probes and rollbacks.
success_criteria: (1) Offline simulator shows mean latency reduction >=5% and 95th percentile not worse than baseline; (2) Online gated rollout with 10% traffic improves token-cost or latency in at least 3 customer workloads without regressions; (3) Probe overhead stays <1% of total tokens and probes respect configured budget; (4) Telemetry surfaces per-arch/seqlen posterior distributions and drift alerts.
steps: Design Bayesian model: priors per (arch, seqlen_bucket, op_variant) with conjugate Beta/Gaussian approximations
Implement microprobe harness: single-request synthetic microbench that executes candidate kernels with KV-cache warm/cold variants
Build offline evaluator: replay production trace segments through simulator to estimate expected regret and probe budget trade-offs
Integrate online controller: Thompson-sampling-based probe scheduler with global probe budget and per-customer safepoints
Add telemetry and rollback hooks: expose posterior snapshots, per-kernel confidence, and automatic rollback if latency regressions detected
Run staged rollout: dev cluster -> canary on low-risk customers -> 10% production -> evaluate and expand
notes: We must account for divergence between synthetic microprobe conditions and multi-tenant production interference; use calibration factor learned from early canaries.
Prefill kernels often benefit from large batch occupancy measurements; decode kernels need per-step latency and KV cache effects modeled separately.
Memory-bound kernels can show false-positive latency wins in single-probe cases; add occupancy-aware features (SM utilization, active warps) to the cost model.
Keep feature vector compact to avoid heavy online inference — we only use (arch_id, seqlen_bucket, kernel_id, kv_state, recent_latency_mean) for decisioning.
comments: 2026-01-22 | Aisha Malik: Kickoff meeting notes attached in drive. Agreed to use Thompson sampling for exploration and a per-arch prior seed from microbenchmarks.
2026-02-05 | Connor Reed: Prototype microprobe harness implemented. Microbench shows divergent latency scaling on Ampere vs Hopper at seqlen > 2048 — added occupancy features.
2026-02-18 | Priya Shah (SRE): Alerting hooks proposed; recommend adding automatic quota throttles to avoid noisy neighbor amplification during probes.
2026-02-27 | Connor Reed: Offline replay on sample traces indicates 6.3% mean token latency improvement and 0.4% probe overhead with beta priors seeded from microbench results.
2026-03-03 | Design Review (PM): Product okayed canary plan but requested clearer rollback criteria and customer-facing opt-out for private deployments.
2026-03-10 | QA: End-to-end tests for probe budget exhaustion and rollback path added. Found a race when multiple probes target same kernel — fixed with per-kernel probe mutex.
2026-03-14 | Connor Reed: Canary rollout started at 5% for internal orgs. First-day telemetry shows posterior concentrating for one kernel on seqlen 512 on A100s; monitoring for regression.
